content:
Section 1 Purpose and Applicability
This matrix defines purchase approval authority for eligible purchase orders issued or closed during its effective period. It does not replace contract, supplier qualification, or competitive-sourcing guidance.
title: Approval Authority Matrix

content:
Section 2 Valid Approval Criteria
A valid PURCHASE approval is recorded as APPROVED on or before the purchase order issuance date. Each required approval must be from a distinct approver. A rejected, withdrawn, pending, late, or duplicate approval does not satisfy this matrix.
title: Approval Authority Matrix

content:
Section 4.2 Purchase Orders Strictly Above USD 75,000
For an eligible purchase order dated during 2025, a total amount strictly greater than USD 75,000 requires two distinct valid PURCHASE approvals, including at least one valid approval by a DIRECTOR. The amount comparison is strict: an amount equal to USD 75,000 is not within this section. The requirement is assessed against the committed purchase order amount and the approval record available at issuance. This section is the authoritative hard approval requirement for the stated scope.
title: Approval Authority Matrix

content:
Section 5 Recordkeeping and Timing
The purchase record must retain the approver identity, role, approval type, status, and timestamp. When approval evidence is unavailable, the record requires review rather than an assumption that no approval occurred. Questions outside this matrix should be escalated to Procurement Governance.

content:
Section 1 Scope and Contract-Required Categories
This policy governs contract coverage for eligible purchase orders. In this MVP, the contract-required categories are IT Services and Professional Services. Other categories may use contracts, but absence of a contract alone is not a failure under this policy.
title: Contract Compliance Policy

content:
Section 4.1 Required Contract Coverage and Approved Exceptions
For an eligible purchase order dated during 2025 in IT Services or Professional Services, a valid contract at issuance is required unless a documented contract exception was approved by a DIRECTOR no later than issuance. A documented, timely Director-approved exception is a permitted substitute for a valid contract for the specific purchase order.
section_title: Required Contract Coverage and Approved Exceptions
title: Contract Compliance Policy

content:
Section 4.2 Valid Contract Evidence
A valid contract is resolved to the purchase order, matches its supplier and category, covers the issuance date, and has not terminated on or before that date. An expired, terminated, mismatched, or unresolved contract reference is not valid contract coverage.
title: Contract Compliance Policy

content:
Section 5 Documentation and Escalation
The purchase record should preserve the contract reference or the documented exception and its approval timing. When contract evidence is unavailable or a reference cannot be resolved, Procurement must investigate the record before a conclusion is made. This policy does not treat supplier concentration as a contract violation.

content:
Section 1 Purpose, Scope, and Governance
This policy establishes common procurement governance for enterprise purchases. It applies to employees who request, approve, select, or administer suppliers. It sets decision principles; the Approval Authority Matrix and Contract Compliance Policy contain the authoritative approval and contract requirements. Procurement records must identify the business need, supplier, category, committed amount, and accountable approver. Purchase commitments are made only through the approved procurement process.
title: Corporate Procurement Policy

content:
Section 2 Purchase Governance
Business owners remain responsible for a clear need, an appropriate supplier recommendation, and a complete purchase record. Procurement may request supporting market, qualification, commercial, or contract information before a commitment is issued. This policy does not create an automated compliance threshold for competitive sourcing. Approval thresholds and timing requirements are governed by the applicable Approval Authority Matrix.
title: Corporate Procurement Policy

content:
Section 3 Competitive Sourcing Guidance
For material purchases, teams should consider competitive alternatives when practical and document the basis for their recommendation. The number of quotations, commercial comparison, and sourcing rationale are human review evidence in this MVP; they are not automatic PASS or FAIL conditions.
title: Corporate Procurement Policy

content:
Section 4 Supplier Selection Principles
Supplier selection should consider capability, qualifications, commercial value, continuity of supply, and category risk. Critical-category concentration and limited alternatives should trigger mitigation discussion, not an automatic policy violation.
title: Corporate Procurement Policy

content:
Section 5 Exceptions and Related Policies
Documented exceptions must be reviewed under the policy that governs the exception type. Contract exceptions are governed by the Contract Compliance Policy. Approval requirements are governed by the Approval Authority Matrix. Where policies conflict, the more specific applicable policy controls.

title: Corporate Procurement Policy

content:
Section 1 Purpose and Qualification
This policy guides supplier selection and ongoing category resilience. Teams should consider supplier capability, required qualifications, commercial suitability, continuity, and the needs of the business unit. Qualification status is evidence for a decision, not a substitute for the applicable approval or contract requirements.
title: Supplier Selection Policy

content:
Section 2 Critical Categories and Limited Alternatives
Critical categories require heightened attention to continuity and alternative sourcing. A category with limited qualified alternatives can create operational risk even where current purchases satisfy approval and contract requirements.
title: Supplier Selection Policy

content:
Section 3 Concentration Mitigation Review
High spend concentration with one qualified supplier should trigger a mitigation review. Teams may document alternatives, transition feasibility, contingency arrangements, or an accepted business rationale. Supplier concentration is a risk finding and is not an automatic compliance FAIL.
title: Supplier Selection Policy

content:
Section 4 Decision Records
The decision record should identify the category, participating suppliers where relevant, qualification considerations, and any mitigation owner. Procurement Governance may request additional review for critical categories, but this policy creates no automated approval threshold or contract rule.
title: Supplier Selection Policy
